_comment: EVERY NON-ZERO NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS AN ESTIMATE. Not one of them has been proved by a --meter run, and treating one as fact is listed under 'Common mistakes' in CLAUDE.md. A vendor's price page is a marketing document; the invoice depends on the resolution actually delivered, the seconds actually billed, and whether a retried submit charged twice. scripts/providers/pricing.mjs REFUSES to load an entry that does not carry a _comment and an explicit `estimate` flag, and refuses `estimate: false` on any non-zero price -- zero is the only price that cannot drift. When actual diverges from estimated by more than divergenceLimit, `npm run ledger` names the job. Believe the ledger, not this file.

fixture/still-v1._comment: Not an estimate, and the only kind of entry allowed to say so: the fixture provider spawns local ffmpeg and there is no counterparty to bill anyone. Zero is a fact here. It is listed rather than special-cased so the cost path -- estimate, record, compare -- is exercised end to end at $0 before a paid provider is ever wired in.

fixture/video-v1._comment: Not an estimate. Same reasoning as fixture/still-v1 -- local ffmpeg, no counterparty, zero is a fact.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/image-to-video._comment: ESTIMATE, and deliberately the CONSERVATIVE one. config/credits.json is the resolution-aware money path -- $1.51 per 15s at 480p, $4.54 at 720p -- and this table has no resolution dimension at all: estimateVideo takes seconds and nothing else. So the number here is the 720p rate, $4.54 / 15s = $0.3027 per second, which OVERSTATES a 480p job by about 3x. That is the safe direction to be wrong in for the same reason credits.json gives: overstating cost understates margin. It is not the number a customer sees -- they see credits, computed by creditCost from credits.json -- it is the number the manifest and npm run ledger carry. One --meter run replaces both.
bytedance/seedance-2.0/image-to-video.source: derived from config/credits.json 720p estimate, itself derived from fal's published token formula, UNVERIFIED

bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-vide._comment: ESTIMATE. Same rate and same reasoning as image-to-video above -- fal prices the two Seedance 2.0 routes off the same token formula as far as anyone has read, and nobody has read an invoice. Listed so that switching the animate step to the two-reference route is a config change rather than an unknown_model at compose.

fal/still-UNVERIFIED._comment: ESTIMATE, and a placeholder: the still model has NOT been chosen. Paul picks it at Phase 0 (docs/phase-0-validation.md), and criterion 6 measures the real number as balance-before minus balance-after. The figure below is an order-of-magnitude stand-in for an identity-preserving image model at ~1MP so the estimator has something to divide by -- it is not a quote and it is not attributed to any vendor. Replace the id and the number together, in one edit, when the model is chosen.
fal/still-UNVERIFIED.source: order-of-magnitude placeholder, no vendor quote, UNVERIFIED

fal/video-UNVERIFIED._comment: ESTIMATE, and a placeholder: the video model has NOT been chosen. Per-second because that is the common shape for image-to-video billing, not because any specific vendor was checked. 15 seconds at this rate is $3.00 per finished video, which is the number that decides whether this product has a price -- so it is exactly the number that must be replaced by a measurement rather than argued about.
fal/video-UNVERIFIED.source: order-of-magnitude placeholder, no vendor quote, UNVERIFIED
